expectation: Membrane/surface stain on scattered antigen-presenting cells (macrophages, DCs, B cells) with dendritic outlines, in lamina propria and follicles; gut epithelium may also show some HLA-DR. Overlap with a subset of CD163 cells.
observed: A: gut tissue with scattered bright yellow cells and a diffuse epithelial lining. B/C: distinct bright cells beside moderate epithelial lining signal. D: a bright cell with a membrane outline. E: dendritic-shaped cells in a CD163-rich field, some overlapping CD163 (white) and some not (green).
why: A distinct population of membrane-stained, dendritic-shaped cells sits partly on CD163 cells as the marker graph predicts, so the epithelial haze does not decide the verdict.
notes: Bright, membrane-localised, dendritic cells form a specific population in the lamina propria. They overlap a subset of CD163 macrophages, and a CD163-negative HLA-DR population (likely DCs or B cells) is also present. The epithelial lining signal is plausible for gut.
